quest.title: Dream of Falling
quest.description: You realize that many people may be experiencing unusual dreams just like Ilman. To prevent the dreams from causing more harm, you must return to "A Moment of Dreams" to take measures.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x750, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look. She's sitting over there... and surrounded by monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's rescue her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She seems to be in the same condition as Ilman earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, but luckily, she hasn't been injured or jolted awake yet. Let's carefully move her somewhere safer.

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: See you tomorrow, Professor Aisha...

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: Hmm... Huh? Wh—Why am I back here again?

choices.text: Nobody else is here.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Dreaming? But what about Professor Aisha...?

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Oh, I see. It was all just a dream... Well, that makes sense. After all, it hasn't changed a single bit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's "it"?

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Nearly twenty years, and it still hasn't bloomed... *sigh*

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Does it have something to do with your dream? Please, tell us what you mean.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Ah, sorry, I'm still feeling a little groggy. Please give me a moment here... Whew.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Ahem, alright, where to start... Right, this plant... So, Professor Aisha gave me this plant just before she left.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: She was a good friend of my parents' and my first real tutor. She was also an outstanding Amurta researcher.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: In addition to her extraordinary academic talents, she was also skilled in combat, and would accept lots of work from the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you mean she's left on an adventure?

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Yes. When I was about ten years old, she told me that she must go look for the secrets of "the Abyss," and that she would be gone for a long time.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: I grabbed hold of her and wouldn't let go. I didn't know what "the Abyss" was... I just knew that she was like family to me.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: She hugged me, and we cried for some time until I fell asleep. When I woke up, I was already back home.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: She still decided to leave, but had left behind a letter for me saying that I was the person she cared for most in this world.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: She claimed that investigating "the Abyss" could help more ordinary people protect the people and things they care about.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: She had obtained some important evidence during her past adventures... If she didn't set off right away, she might miss the perfect opportunity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess "ad astra abyssosque" isn't just a slogan...

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: She left a seed in the letter, telling me that if it sprouted and bloomed, then she'd come back, no matter what sort of risky situation she was in.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: She said she looked forward to seeing me all grown up...

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: But strangely, I've tried watering it, feeding it, everything I could think of... but I've never been able to get it to bloom.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: I even went to ask the Amurta researchers, and they couldn't explain it, either.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: May I have a look at the plant?

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Of course. I was hoping the great Dendro Archon could help me solve this problem.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Let me see. Hmm, oh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, we've never seen that look on Nahida's face before.

choices.text: (Wait, could it be...!?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sh—She looks a little unwell. Um, hold on, we'll be right back!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong, Nahida? You can't tell what's wrong with the plant, either?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: No, I immediately understood what's happening with that plant... I'm just not sure if I should say it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This plant is not known to the academic world. It's a new species that her teacher managed to cultivate by some special means.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Judging by its features, I can tell from the moment it sprouted, it'll never be able to bloom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: I—It can't be...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It means that this "Professor Aisha" she keeps mentioning might have foreseen the danger, and was prepared to never return.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: From my experience observing people, she would undoubtedly regard this as a "brutal" revelation.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: When forced to confront such "brutal" truths, people may break down into tears, talk nonsense, or lose their tempers...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #I know she has to face the truth, but at the same time, I don't want to hurt her... Tell me, {NICKNAME}, what should I do?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's a tricky one... Seems like you've already got a good idea of the feelings she might experience.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll tell her.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But wouldn't that mean I'm just pushing it all on you? What if she just gets angry at you instead?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's all right. There are all kinds of people, and the examples you observed are just the most extreme cases.

choices.text: I've seen many situations like this before.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: O—Okay... Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go back and tell her.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Huh! It'll never bloom!?

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: But how's that possible? If a plant is unable to bloom, doesn't that mean it can't reproduce, either? All that's left for it to do is slowly wither away!

choices.text: It seems like that may be exactly what your teacher intended.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Are you saying... she never intended to return? Seriously? So everything she said was a lie...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she meant well! Since the separation was inevitable, she hoped that you would be able to come to grips with such a cruel parting a little later in life.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She really cared about you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Her love, care, and attention to you... All those warm moments were real.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I guess she had hoped that you could understand and respect her choice after learning the truth.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: ...I see. Sorry, I don't want to sound ungrateful, but it's just... just so much to take in.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: The dreams are so beautiful, yet reality is heartlessly cold.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: I really thought she had come back. I had so much to tell her...

choices.text: I can understand your grief.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: These dreams may not be as pure and beautiful as they seem. Some kind of power may be exploiting your feelings.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: R—Really?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. So with that in mind, until our investigation is completed, please return to the event and ignore any further temptations from your dreams.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: I see, thank you for rescuing me and sorry for the trouble. Luckily, the plant didn't get hurt either.

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Otherwise, I wouldn't have anything left to remember her by.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thanks, Traveler and Paimon. She seems to have finally accepted the truth, but I think she'll still need a long time to come to terms with her feelings.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I saw her waver the moment you mentioned love.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It was almost like a gentle rain, arriving just in time to put out a fire that was about to spread.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's because people have something called "empathy."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: "Empathy"? Hmm, I see... This is valuable knowledge indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, you said there may be something that's trying to exploit their feelings. Any idea what that might be?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. What's common between Ilman and Kathya's cases is that they've both lost someone dear to them.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And now... they get to meet the people they cherish in their dreams again, and the people feel more real than anything a regular dream could hope to create.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Instead of interpreting it as a result of their longing, I have to consider a more antagonistic explanation... Someone is taking advantage of their longing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But what would be the motive?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, they're just causing these people to dream. What are they after?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This is exactly what we need to investigate. Anyway, let's pay another visit to "A Moment of Dreams."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I have a bad feeling about all of this... I hope things haven't gotten any worse.

choices.text: We're trying to investigate these dreams.
She meant to convey a message through the plant's true nature.
There's always a way to work through it.
(An expression pleading for help?)
You were dreaming just now.

talks.objective: Return to "A Moment of Dreams" again

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We're back. How's everything here?

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Uh, I am so sorry, great Dendro Archon. We're still trying to figure out how to explain the whole thing to everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Because of your warning, we've brought dreamers here even if they were completely unaware of the danger.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: But some of them have already fallen asleep, and they haven't woken up for a long time. I fear there's nothing we can do about it.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: "A Moment of Dreams" is just a small interest group... We don't have enough staff members to handle this.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Just as I expected, it seems my guess was correct.

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: It's the Dendro Archon. She's back!

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: What happened? Why have we been gathered here?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Many of you here have been experiencing some beautiful dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But I'm sorry to tell you that based on our investigation, there's some kind of conspiracy behind them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Before we learn the truth, please don't try to recreate the scenes in your dreams. Whatever you see, don't be tempted by them.

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: I don't think it's a big deal. Aren't we just dreaming? It's not like dreams will have an effect on others.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We've already met two people who ran off to the countryside alone and got caught in dangerous situations by falling to the temptations in their dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! These aren't just dreams — it's serious!

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: All right... I get it, I get it.

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: So does that mean once we have some conclusive results from the investigation, we can continue to enjoy these dreams?

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: Yeah, I still want to visit my sister in my dreams...

choices.text: No, not necessarily.

response.speaker: Nasser
response.text: I'm sorry if what I'm about to say sounds a little offensive, great Dendro Archon, but...

response.speaker: Nasser
response.text: We had a discussion with the folks who just arrived here... In all of our dreams, we were able to reunite with people who were very close to us.

response.speaker: Nasser
response.text: They all seemed as if they were alive again, which makes us reluctant to wake up.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, that's also what we've observed in our investigation.

response.speaker: Nasser
response.text: So, if the results of this investigation would mean an end to those dreams, that'd be quite cruel to us.

response.speaker: Nasser
response.text: All of us understand the danger, but... perhaps you can't quite understand just how much those people mean to us.

response.speaker: Nasser
response.text: I don't think everyone will be on board with the plan to abandon these dreams for good.

response.speaker: Nasser
response.text: Before the conclusion of the investigation, they'll at least want to meet the people in their dreams one last time and say goodbye.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: We've never had such a difficult situation before. It appears that not many people are willing to cooperate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So they still want to return to their dreams despite knowing the danger?

choices.text: It's hard to clearly say who's right and who's wrong here.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's right. Compared with these sweet and beautiful dreams, our warnings of danger are dull and emotionless... It looks like the situation will inevitably spiral out of control.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The more time we waste, the more people will ignore our warnings and return to their alluring dreams.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what should we do?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Seems we have to go into a dream and find out the truth for ourselves.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Pedrush, is there anyone here who's experiencing a marvelous dream right now?

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Ah, let me think... Yes, this way.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Good, please take us there.

choices.text: Everyone has their own perspectives.
It will depend on the results of our investigation.

talks.objective: Follow Pedrush to check on the person who is currently dreaming

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: Actually, I can really sympathize with everyone's feelings on this.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hmm, she's only asleep and hasn't started sleepwalking... It seems she hasn't sunk too deep into her dream yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do we also need to fall asleep if we want to go into her dream?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't worry about that. I'm Lesser Lord Kusanali, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Now, don't be nervous. Just close your eyes... imagine yourselves as waves gradually rolling onto the beach.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You slowly wash over the shore and sink into the sand...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, this place looks familiar! Isn't it Puspa Café?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon sees Debbi. She's right over there! Looks like we've come to the right place.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: These alluring dreams often portray a scene from real life, which concurs with our previous findings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? But what about that space we were in just now?

choices.text: Maybe it was like some kind of hub.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can't mean... this is another collective dream!?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, given that so many people have been experiencing these beautiful dreams, I would say it's very likely that they're interconnected.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Compared to an interconnected dream, independent individual dreams would be much harder to manage and manipulate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon gets it now... Well, let's go talk with Debbi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, but there are some other people next to her. Are they dreaming, too?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If this space is exclusive to Debbi's dream, then the others beside her are most likely the people she cherishes.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, we should confirm that first, just to be sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? How do we do that?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Just leave it to me.

choices.text: The dreams may be connected.

talks.objective: Talk to Nahida to understand the situation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Traveler? You look a little disoriented.

choices.text: ...No, it's nothing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, okay. Just remember that Paimon is always here for you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, seems like we've made it into the dream!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm, I thought we would arrive at some familiar scene, but we seem to have landed in a completely unfamiliar place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, so many giant plants, even in the sky. Amazing...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Theoretically, we should have gone straight into Debbi's dream. Things do seem to have gone a bit sideways here...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, let's see if we can find any leads.

choices.text: It seems this whole dream situation is getting to me, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Paimon didn't notice anything...

talks.objective: Enter the depths of the dream

dialogues.speaker: Emira
dialogues.text: You know, I've heard that plants grow better if you play music for them.

dialogues.speaker: Emira
dialogues.text: And on that note, it's been a while since I last heard you play.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Sorry, I've been a little busy these last couple days.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Oh, the Dendro Archon... What a pleasant surprise!

dialogues.speaker: Emira
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh! Welcome, great Dendro Archon! And your companions, too, welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Emira
dialogues.text: I'm Emira. I run the flower shop here. And this is my husband, Moseis.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Yes, how may we help you?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You already know all about me. There's no need for all the pleasantries.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should call you, "the dream's owner"?

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Hahaha, as expected of the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Emira. It seems my research has attracted the Dendro Archon's attention.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Why don't you go back to the flower shop, I'll come help you a little later.

dialogues.speaker: Emira
dialogues.text: Okay, of course, dear. I'll see you later.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: It appears that I was too naive to think I could deceive the Dendro Archon in person like this.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: To avoid looking like too much of a fool, allow me to ask the first question: How well would you say you understand this dream?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This dream was built by the Akasha, and it has the power to create imaginary people who no longer exist in the real world.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As for you... you've found a unique way to become the owner of this dream, going so far as to have even given up the ability to wake up again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Given up... the ability to wake up?

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Hahaha, impressive! You truly are the embodiment of wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Please, tell me how you were able to arrive at such a conclusion. In return, I'll answer the question you're most curious about.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's simple. Apart from you, this space only consists of real people who are dreaming and imaginary people who were created here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Although you are here and appear no different from the others, I can't sense your dream.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: How can I wake up a person who's already awake?

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Since you're the fully awake owner of this dream, it can never collapse from you waking up.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Theoretically, this should also give you absolute control over this place. I have to admit, it really doesn't get much better than that.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But even knowing all of that, one question remains: How did you do it?

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Isn't the answer right in front of you, great Dendro Archon? It's because I've dedicated my entire reality to this dream.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: I uploaded my entire consciousness into the Akasha when it was still running.

choices.text: Your entire consciousness?

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Actually, this all started because of an accident. My original goal was not about the Akasha or a collective dream...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: No, you were motivated above all to create a hyper-realistic "person"... The desire to reconnect with a "real" loved one is the one shared sentiment between all our dreamers.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: That's right. However, human models are too complicated. Only the Akasha has a Jnana Energy supply powerful enough for me to generate and sustain my models.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: The Akasha is truly magnificent. If I siphoned a minuscule amount of its energy, nobody would even notice. And even this "minuscule" amount of energy was already more than enough for my purposes.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Even using just crude methods, I was still able to train a fairly realistic person.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: I named my first work "Emira."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You mean the girl we just saw!?

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: She and I entered the Akademiya on the same day. Starting with admission procedures, we bumped into each other six times on just that first day.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: And because of that one day, we eventually went on to fall in love. We studied, conducted research, and made breakthroughs together.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Our rhythm was always in step. I felt like we were two separate bodies that shared the same heart...

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: However, Eleazar later took her from me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you're gathering others like you.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Yes, I need more training samples to perfect Emira's personality.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: I found their details in the Akasha's database. Using the pretext of testing for mental health disorders, I implanted signaling devices in their bodies.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: This way, I could connect them to a network, and Emira could feel their yearning. Little by little, they helped her to grow and develop a warm, human personality.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: To improve my efficiency and allow myself to focus on nothing but my research, I uploaded my consciousness as well, and became a part of the network.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm, so technically speaking, it's not that you won't wake up — it's that you can't wake up.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Yes. Because the Akasha was suddenly turned off, I lost all of my Jnana Energy. I became imprisoned in the very network I had constructed.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: At first, I panicked. But, after coming to grips with the situation, I realized that I could restart this world as long as I could find a replacement source of Jnana Energy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means... everyone in the network is providing you with Jnana Energy!

choices.text: That's insane...

talks.objective: Look for clues in the café

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, glad that's over...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But what happened just now?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He's not very proficient in using the Akasha's technology, and he spent a lot of Jnana Energy creating monsters. Now the system is out of control.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: All the people he created also turned into monsters, including Emira.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's terrible, even for a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even Paimon's freaked out. Paimon can't imagine what they're going through.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's like a horrible nightmare.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The good news is that the chaos seems to have subsided.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Now we only need to wake up the people here, and let them return to their real lives.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Emira, my dear Emira...

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: They're all gone. It was just a big dream after all.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: I couldn't change my fate, and my knowledge turned out to be useless. What a cruel world...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Do you still think this is our fault?

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: I don't care about that anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: The Jnana Energy used to sustain this dream has all been transformed into monsters. This dream will soon collapse, and my consciousness along with it.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Let me disappear with Emira... I'd rather turn into dust than to ever wake up again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems that everything that's happened is too much for him. He's lost all hope.

choices.text: I want to say that he's only getting what he deserves...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I think seeing Emira turn into a monster was punishment enough for him.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: After comprehending the hollowness of the unreal, it's time to revisit the meaning of existence.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Existence? Heh, I'm different from the others. I've long given up everything outside of my consciousness.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Using my knowledge of the Akasha, I have a way to extract your consciousness from here and put it inside a knowledge capsule.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The Akademiya has probably kept your body, so you should be able to wake up soon.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: No need... Just let me disappear. Reality means nothing to me now.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This isn't compassion. I won't let you escape your punishment by simply disappearing.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As for your life after that, it will be up to you how you want to exist.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Alright, Traveler and Paimon. We should go back.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: We can finally wrap up this whole thing...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong, Nahida?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh, nothing. Let's tell the people here to gather at "A Moment of Dreams" after they wake up.

choices.text: But I can't help but also feel sorry for him.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the café

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (Huh, how could they be...?)

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (Well, I guess it doesn't matter...)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: (Huh? She sounds a little hesitant.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I've confirmed that this dream belongs only to Debbi. Because, I'm unable to hear the thoughts of the other two people with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, this is the power of the Dendro Archon...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon had better watch her thoughts from now on.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't worry. I don't often use my powers like this... It's rather impolite.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Alright, I need to get myself ready... It won't be easy to break it to her, but there's no avoiding it now.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Th—The great Dendro Archon! Uh, what brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm sorry to interrupt your celebration, but... have you noticed that what's happening here doesn't quite match up with your memories?

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: I—I don't quite understand, great Dendro Archon... What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Basimah
dialogues.text: I get it. The Dendro Archon is trying to say that it's a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that we're able to gather here.

dialogues.speaker: Gaspar
dialogues.text: Hey, how about a cup of coffee for all of you, my treat! We just returned from a fruitful adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Memories, a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Think carefully. You of all people should know what really happened to them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Are you sure that meeting here and chatting the day away like this isn't just a product of your own wishful thinking?

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Yes, the reports from "The Steambird" were true... The ship they were on struck a reef and sank.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: And I never heard from Basimah and Gaspar again...

dialogues.speaker: Basimah
dialogues.text: Hey, c'mon now. What're you talking about, Debbi?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, trust your memories... Nothing you see here is real.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: I get it now. This is a dream, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: But since it's my dream, it doesn't matter if this is real or not. I enjoy the way things are here... I no longer have to face the tragedies of real life.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: These friends mean the world to me. Nobody else can understand me like they do.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: There's nothing wrong with continuing this dream, is there?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm worried that if you were to continue dreaming like this, the lines between dreams and reality will gradually become too blurred for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: These dreams will always give you what you want, while reality remains full of pain and difficult situations... If you're not careful, you can get hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I still have control. I won't let it go that far.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Gaspar
dialogues.text: Hey, how about we put all this troublesome stuff aside and get back to our coffee and snacks, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Gaspar
dialogues.text: Whether it's just a dream or real life, you should be happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can't just brush off something like this! We don't even know how you people got here, or where you even came from...

choices.text: Don't push it, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, sorry! Paimon didn't mean to upset anyone.

response.speaker: Debbi
response.text: No, it's alright. I understand that you're just trying to look out for me.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It seems that for now, this place is still relatively harmless for you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But I wonder if there's any way to go deeper into the dream...

response.speaker: Debbi
response.text: Huh, now that you mention it, I once heard a strange voice tell me that there's an entrance here.

response.speaker: Debbi
response.text: I'm not interested in checking it out at the moment, but maybe I'll go in and have a look later.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Okay, thanks for your help.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Just as I expected, we're only on the surface of this dream. Let's go.

choices.text: These are important people to Debbi.

talks.objective: Go to the deeper part of the dream

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What are we doing here again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second!? We were just up there, no... down there... Uh, did we go up or down?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't panic, this is how dreams work.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We've left Debbi's dream, but the dream is still continuing onward. I'm not sure where it'll lead us.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This dream has the ability to create imaginary people, which is why people are so unwilling to wake up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If it weren't for what we just saw, Paimon might still find that a bit hard to believe...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So what awaits us further in the dream?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I have a guess. If these dreams are connected, then there should be some sort of order to them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The fact that Debbi was able to realize that she was dreaming means that she is not very deep in the dream yet.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But the space we're in has been turned upside down. Do you remember the characteristics of dreams that I mentioned earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh right! Dreams are chaotic!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's right. It's possible that we're heading deeper into this dream now, and the deeper we go, the closer we'll get to the essence of the dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, so the answers might be waiting for us deeper in the dream.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, and we should get ready for whatever we may encounter.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: The coffee here still tastes the same as ever, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: You two have traveled all around Teyvat. Surely, you've all tasted better coffee than this.

dialogues.speaker: Gaspar
dialogues.text: I suppose so, but no matter how good things may be elsewhere, nothing beats the taste of home.

dialogues.speaker: Basimah
dialogues.text: That's right! It's hard to change your tastes.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Anyway, here's to your return home! Welcome back, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, weren't we already here a little earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This is probably Ilman's dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why would he start dreaming again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Didn't we warn him?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, but it seems that the danger isn't enough to stop him from longing for his wife.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Based on what we've learned so far, he must be sleeping more deeply for his dream to appear here.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But fortunately, he already knows us from before, so hopefully we'll be able to wake him up.

talks.objective: Look for clues near the cliff

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilman!

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you! Incredible, I didn't know you would appear in my dream too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you say dream? Wait, so you know this is a dream!?

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Of course, such good things rarely happen to me in real life these days.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Here, let me introduce everyone. This is Maynar, my wife who I mentioned before, and this is our daughter, Haydar.

dialogues.speaker: Maynar
dialogues.text: Hello, it's a great honor to meet the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Haydar
dialogues.text: Whoa, Dad, you know the Dendro Archon!? That's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Haydar
dialogues.text: And what's this? *gasp* Is it a new toy!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, it's Paimon! Not a toy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, now's not the time for that! Nahida, this doesn't seem to add up with what we were expecting.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hmm, you're right. Let me think for a bit here...

choices.text: Ilman, did you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! We didn't see him in "A Moment of Dreams" earlier. Paimon thought he'd gone home!

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Sorry, I just had to make sure that Haydar could get a chance to see her mother.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I had gotten pretty familiar with the hike, so I brought Haydar with me. I'm just glad we didn't meet any monsters along the way.

response.speaker: Maynar
response.text: Yes, I'm glad too. I didn't expect her to grow up so fast.

response.speaker: Maynar
response.text: It must have been very hard for him. I regret not being able to fulfill my role as a wife and a mother.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: No, don't talk like that. Let's leave all that unhappy stuff behind for now. Even if we're in a dream, it's still a blessing that we've been able to reunite in this way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What should we do now? Should we... tell him the truth?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You can... You can let me break the news. I should... be the one to do it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm sorry, but I should tell you that your dream did not create us. We are real people with our own consciousness.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Like the last time we met, we're still investigating this dream, and we've already learned some things about it.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: So you mean, there's something nefarious with this dream as well?

response.speaker: Maynar
response.text: Hmm? Ilman, what's going on?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: It seems the reunion of our family is destined to only be temporary.

response.speaker: Haydar
response.text: Huh? Is Mom leaving?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Maybe... But in all likelihood, that is indeed how things will end.

response.speaker: Haydar
response.text: No, Mom, you can't leave!

response.speaker: Maynar
response.text: I'm afraid I don't quite understand what's going on...

response.speaker: Maynar
response.text: Don't worry, Haydar. Mom's not going anywhere. Please don't cry.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Maynar doesn't understand any of this.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I'm fully aware that this is a dream, so that's why I've never told her the truth, but...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Never mind. It's not like I would know what to say...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I mean, I don't get any of the complicated stuff, but regardless of whether this dream is good or bad, you're here to resolve it, right?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Then please, let us enjoy this moment for just a while longer.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Regardless of whatever caused this dream to come to pass, I feel extremely grateful to have had the chance to reunite with my family.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: But, does this dream... really have to disappear?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm afraid so. Sorry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Okay, I see...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Please, come this way. You can go even deeper into the dream by heading in this direction.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I have heard that the further down you go, the more pleasant the dreams become... and the more you want to stay.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: The answer you're looking for may also be found there. Go ahead.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thank you for helping us, and I'm truly sorry.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: You're welcome. It's not like I have any say in the matter. I'm just an ordinary person, after all. Who am I to interfere with the work of a god?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I'll be right behind you. I should at least let Maynar and Haydar know what's going on here.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Otherwise, my daughter might be mad at her mother after we wake up...

choices.text: Secretly go back to that place again on your own?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's the same place again... This place is almost like a flight of stairs that connects all the dreams together!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But they appear to be getting more and more aggressive. Regular stairs wouldn't try to attack us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's recap what we've learned so far.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, something seems to be off about our theory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ilman is clearly aware that he's dreaming, and he's enjoying it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rather than dreaming on a deeper level, he almost seemed... more awake?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I believe we're on the right track, but we just need another explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's not that the dreams are getting deeper, it's the owners' attachment to the dreams that's getting stronger.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But you would never mistake dreams for real life, right?

choices.text: Of course not.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sometimes, Paimon almost wishes her dreams could be real!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it's just a quick thought... It's not long before Paimon's thinking about other things... like Sticky Honey Roast.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Listen, we're real beings living in the real world, and that's where our focus should be.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This also explains the insubstantiality of our dreams. No matter what they may become, we don't really care.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But if we decide to abandon reality and embrace our dreams, then our dreams would become far more substantial.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Wait, Paimon's starting to get it now!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Your mind will begin to build the dream far more attentively, which in turn will make it feel more real.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Do you remember how the Akasha can turn dreams into Jnana Energy?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Constructing a realistic dream consumes a similar energy.

choices.text: Which means...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does that mean there's a "host" of these dreams here like Nilou during the Sabzeruz Festival?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we wake that person up, this collective dream will end, right?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mm-hmm, most likely.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But the collective dream in Sumeru City was created by the Akasha, and now the Akasha has been turned off.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This has nothing to do with the Aranara, and humans are not capable of creating a collective dream, which means...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The host has something to do with the Akasha.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? So, did someone manage to restart the Akasha?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mmm... That's impossible, but they are probably a scholar of the Akademiya who had a close connection with the Akasha.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Even so... How did they manage to do it, and how did they choose the host?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's keep moving.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yeah, we haven't gotten to the end yet.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Once we know their motive, all the questions will resolve themselves.

choices.text: There's another dream out there that's responsible for this.
Although sometimes, I almost wish I could.

talks.objective: Reach the deepest part of the dream

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, a new place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, well, it's just new to Paimon in this dream...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This should be the final destination.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's more ordinary than I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, these are just ordinary city streets.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I have powers related to dreams, so it's usually easy for me to tell who's dreaming and who's created by dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I guess only those who have thoroughly accepted this dream will be able to come here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are so many people here. How can we find the host?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I have a way.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the city

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: That's all there really is to it. I don't think I'm doing anything wrong — I'm just saving them as well as myself.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: I provide a beautiful dream, and in return, I harvest their Jnana Energy as fuel for the dream.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: They can wake up anytime they wish. People need to sleep anyway, so why not have some beautiful dreams while they rest?

dialogues.speaker: Anisah
dialogues.text: I agree. This is the home we spent a great deal of effort on to build for ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Kian
dialogues.text: Yeah, she's right. We are staying here of our own free will.

dialogues.speaker: Maynar
dialogues.text: I don't understand this at all, but I just want to spend some more time with my family. I don't want them to be sad.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: ...Thank you, dear. Great Dendro Archon, I hope you can understand.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: You don't need to gather around here. It's alright.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: The great Dendro Archon is nothing if not kind and considerate towards her people. She won't interfere with what we're doing here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh, now he's playing dirty...

choices.text: (He used the imaginary people he created to influence the real people.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It seems like I won't need you to answer my last question.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You're willing to tell me all your secrets because you have nothing to fear.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If you use real people as your weapon and turn them against their archon, then there's nothing the archon can do.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: They just want to be with the people they cherish. I don't think there's anything wrong with me providing them with that opportunity.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: They don't wish to eternally part with their spouses and friends. What's so wrong about that?

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: If you understood humans a little better or had also experienced firsthand the absolute devastation of loss, then perhaps you wouldn't be so cold towards us.

choices.text: She's not cold at all.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If you had used your talents and determination for a just cause, you could have become a sage of the new generation.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Unfortunately, you've committed one of the six cardinal sins of the Akademiya by "attempting the forbidden and fearing none."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You equated people's feelings with cold Jnana Energy and deprived them of the pain that they have to face.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You lured them into these dreams, and even now remain completely unaware of how evil all of this truly is.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Pain? Luring? Those kinds of things haven't existed here from the moment this world was created.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: She's right here. This is Ilman's child, Haydar.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Huh? My daughter? What's wrong with her?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This dream relies on a set network, which means that only those with devices planted in their bodies can enter this world.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Carefully think back and retrace your steps.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I... secretly went back to the mountainside with Haydar. Maynar was already there waiting for me, and Haydar was able to see her mother...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Ah...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: You mean... she isn't actually the real Haydar?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: No, because unlike you, she can't enter this dream.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The moment you came into this dream, it created a "Haydar" to realize your wish of reuniting with your family.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So, tell me: Where's the real Haydar?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: She's still out there on the mountainside...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's right. And she must have been terrified to see her father not in his right mind.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Not to mention the monsters in that area... The situation is very dangerous.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: If Haydar's still out there, then...

response.speaker: Haydar
response.text: What're you talking about, Dad? I don't understand.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I must wake up right now! I can't leave her there alone.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It seems the others have also remembered something.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: People try to avoid pain and stay in their perceived bubbles of safety out of an instinct to protect themselves. This is human nature, but it is also one of their weaknesses.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: However, why are there still so many people striving to move forward even when they know the path ahead is dangerous and painful?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's because people don't only live for themselves.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: They have families, loved ones, friends, and communities. They have dreams that they are still trying to achieve.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But in this dream, you showed them only the most comfortable and soothing things. This entire world has been built on a foundation of buried and unseen pain.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's all just a well-devised scam.

response.speaker: Kian
response.text: It seems like I've stayed in the dream for too long.

response.speaker: Thana
response.text: I still have so many things I haven't done...

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Heh, I thought gods didn't understand humans. That would have explained why they created such a flawed world, where countless tragedies took place.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: I didn't expect you to arrive at the answer through sheer power of observation... But, unfortunately, it means nothing now.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: If you wanted to spend a little time in the waking world, go right ahead. In any case, I wanted to spend some time alone with Emira.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: As long as this dream continues to exist, you'll come back.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: Humans aren't as strong as you think. Even if you're a god, they won't always listen to you.

response.speaker: Moseis
response.text: It's time to purge all the extraneous data and noise.

choices.text: You don't know the first thing about her.
(He turned the real dreamers against us.)

talks.objective: The dream is out of control

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Haydar...

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: It's just sleepwalking, they're really overreacting.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: *yawn* I'm getting really sleepy.

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: It's just a dream. How bad could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: What's all the sudden commotion about?

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: Sorry, I might have spoken a little out of turn just now.

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: I just think that the gods really don't understand us sometimes...

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: It's hard to talk them into coming here. What's happening is way beyond us.

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: All this commotion is making me wish I could experience this kind of dream, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way, not on Paimon's watch!

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: Alright, alright... No need to get so worked up.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: I think I need a moment to calm down.

dialogues.speaker: Gaspar
dialogues.text: Hey, what's with the sad face?

dialogues.speaker: Basimah
dialogues.text: Yeah, there's no need to worry about all that complicated stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: You go right on ahead, I'll catch up with you later.

dialogues.speaker: Haydar
dialogues.text: Cheer up, Dad... And Mommy, too.

dialogues.speaker: Maynar
dialogues.text: Thank you, Haydar... my baby.

dialogues.speaker: Kian
dialogues.text: It's a bit noisy today, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Anisah
dialogues.text: Huh, you think so? I don't feel anything out of the ordinary.

dialogues.speaker: Kian
dialogues.text: Oh, maybe you're right. It's always been quite peaceful here.

dialogues.speaker: Inas
dialogues.text: What should I buy? Hey, tell me what you think, Shadiyah.

dialogues.speaker: Shadiyah
dialogues.text: How about this? I think it would really suit you.

dialogues.speaker: Inas
dialogues.text: Let me have a look... Oh, it looks great.

dialogues.speaker: Haydar
dialogues.text: Wow, what a beautiful place. Look Mom, the scenery is so pretty here!

dialogues.speaker: Maynar
dialogues.text: Be careful. Don't fall now.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Oh, hey! Seems we somehow managed to get here before you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How did you beat us here? Didn't you have to go through that super crazy confusing place?

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Uh, I'm not sure what you're talking about... All we did was walk through that passageway, and here we are.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We're in a dream. The concept of fixed spaces doesn't always apply here.

dialogues.speaker: Thana
dialogues.text: It's not going to rain soon, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Rakesh
dialogues.text: Then maybe we should head home? I don't wanna get rained on.

dialogues.speaker: Thana
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's wait for the weather to get better before we head back out again. It's not like we're in a rush or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Emira
dialogues.text: Remember to come to the flower shop later. I've got a surprise for you.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Oh, sure thing, Emira. I'll be over as soon as I'm done with this.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Heh, you haven't won just yet

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: This lady refused to heed our warnings and fell asleep here a little earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: (Even if the gods can sense our pain, they can't understand how fragile we truly are.)

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: (Hold it together now... Don't panic.)

dialogues.speaker: Kathya
dialogues.text: (What's so wrong about a beautiful dream?)

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: (...I can't help but be really curious, though. Just what are these dreams...?)

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (What an amazing aroma...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, a door? Hmm, wonder where it could lead...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's not like we have any other way to go now. Let's go in and have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (*sigh* It's all just a dream...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, it looks like we may need to put something inside there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Are we back up here again? Ah wait, Paimon's confused! Are we up here or down there!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, good thing we didn't fall, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes we did, we just fell upwards.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not helping, Nahida! Ugh, Paimon has no clue what's going on anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, when it rains, it seems to disappear slowly.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, and it appears again as soon as the rain stops. It's less like a flower, and more like a Dendro Slime that's trying to keep out of sight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, here we go again with Nahida's analogies...

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: (Is this too cruel for Haydar? How can I ever get her to come to terms with this...?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're not doing something bad... are we, Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That depends on how you define "good" and "bad."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All the water that used to be here has turned into rain.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Then let's get through here before the water level rises.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've finally made it. The destination is right ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Kian
dialogues.text: (Anisah is always so calm... I wish I were the same.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He's just in an ordinary dream, so it shouldn't be him.

dialogues.speaker: Inas
dialogues.text: (Shadiyah has such good taste. I can never go wrong with her opinion.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No, it doesn't seem to be her.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: (Who doesn't want a dream to last forever...?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He's just entered the dream recently. It's definitely not him.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: However... Hm...

dialogues.speaker: Thana
dialogues.text: (Sometimes I wish Rakesh could be more assertive, but... I guess I'm also happy enough with the way things are.)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No, it's not her, unfortunately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, monsters! Be careful!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: All of you, please get out of here and find somewhere safe!

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: I am the master of this dream. I can create endless waves of monsters with the snap of a finger.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: Don't worry. They'll wake up before they get hurt. Emira doesn't like to see others in pain.

dialogues.speaker: Moseis
dialogues.text: If you know what's good for you, leave now.

dialogues.speaker: Anisah?
dialogues.text: Ahhhhh, just shut up, ■■!

dialogues.speaker: Shadiyah?
dialogues.text: ■■■, just decide for yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Haydar?
dialogues.text: ■■, what should I do? Where did ■■ go?

dialogues.speaker: Maynar?
dialogues.text: ■■■ left because he doesn't want you anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Rakesh?
dialogues.text: ■■, stop bossing me around!

dialogues.speaker: Emira?
dialogues.text: ■■■, get away from there! Don't ruin my flowers!

dialogues.speaker: Emira?
dialogues.text: Who... am I? I'm... not Emira. I'm ■■■.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: (Haydar...)

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (Why am I so sleepy...?)

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: (So some people are having pretty realistic dreams, big deal. What are they so worried about?)

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: (What happened? I need to ask someone and find out.)
